From: Dana Collins <dana.collins@carverhealth.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: p95 spike after v7z rollout — immediate impact to API SLAs

Aditya,

We pushed your latest model (v7z) in the 02:00 UTC rollout window last night and are now seeing a consistent p95 jump on our critical /generate route from ~220ms to ~1.2s. This is causing timeouts in our customer-facing search flow. We attached a short perf snapshot and the canary logs — you can see rising tail latency starting around 01:50 UTC.

This is an urgent SLA issue for us (we're on the Business plan with a 500ms p95 commitment). Please advise: we need either an immediate rollback to the previous model variant or a documented mitigation plan and confirmation on credits for the missed SLA.

Attached: perf_report_20270502.pdf, canary-logs-7z-20270503.tar.gz

Thanks,
Dana Collins
Head of Platform
Carver Health

Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: p95 spike after v7z rollout — immediate impact to API SLAs

Dana — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. I'm looping in Lauren (CS), Vivek (SRE/Infra), and Priyom (Ops) to triage. Short plan from our side:

- Triage + confirm root cause (Vivek) — priority 1.
- If root cause is correlated to model v7z performance profile we’ll perform a rollback to v7y in the same region, starting a canary then full rollback (Priyom).
- We will propose a one-week service credit while we finish the rollback and verification; will confirm scope and amount after internal signoff.

Can everyone confirm ETA for rollback or if alternative mitigations (burst routing to alternate pool, temporary q4 quantization profile) are viable? Dana, I’ll update you within 60 minutes with the immediate action.

—Aditya

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: p95 spike after v7z rollout — immediate impact to API SLAs

Quick tech summary from the canary logs (high level):

- Observed: sudden increase in per-token latency on sequences > 128 tokens originating from region us-west-2 after v7z activation at 01:48 UTC.
- Root cause hypothesis: v7z introduced a different attention kernel path that degrades with longer context due to suboptimal kernel selection on our current GPU driver.
- Evidence: 3 canary hosts show KV cache flush frequency increased (see canary-logs-7z-20270503.tar.gz); CPU-side batching queuing rose ~30%.

Recommended immediate actions:
1) Initiate canary rollback to v7y on one host (ETA 12 min) and monitor p95 on the same traffic slice.
2) If canary improves p95 to baseline, proceed with staged global rollback (ETA 45–60 min).
3) If rollback not possible within 45 min, enable temporary routing to dedicated fallback pool running v7x (capacity permitting).

I support a temporary SLA carveout while we complete rollback verification — we should document start/end windows and credit calculation. Priyom, can you prepare the rollback jobs and confirm runbook?

—Vivek
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: p95 spike after v7z rollout — immediate impact to API SLAs

Aditya / team — rollback runbook prepared, checklist below. We can kick off canary rollback now on us-west-2. Estimated timeline:

- 00:00–00:12: Canary rollback deploy to 1 host (validation on p95)
- 00:12–00:40: Staged rollback to remaining canaries / 20% traffic slice
- 00:40–01:10: Full rollout to region if validation green

I will attach the rollback job manifest to the ticket after kick-off. Regarding credits: recommend the standard pro-rated one-week credit for production SLA misses while rollback verifies — we’ll surface exact token counts for finance.

Canary logs and perf artifacts will be appended to INF-7123 as they appear.

—Priyom
Platform Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

Dana — immediate update and next steps: we initiated the canary rollback to v7y at 09:30 PT (01:30 UTC). Early results: the affected traffic slice saw p95 move from ~1.2s down to ~240ms within the canary window. Priyom will continue staged rollback; target full regional rollback within ~60 minutes from now.

We will:
- Complete rollback and verify p95 across the region.
- Issue a pro-rated service credit equal to one week of your monthly plan for the SLA breach window (formal credit calculation and DocuSign will follow).
- Open INF-7123 for forensic artifacts (canary logs + perf_report_20270502.pdf attached).

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep this thread updated every 30 minutes until closure.

Thanks for the quick flag, Dana.

—Aditya
